title: Taal Volcano Eruption
script: Taal Volcano in the Philippines began to erupt on January 12, 2020, with a phreatomagmatic eruption from its main crater. The eruption sent ashes over Calabarzon, Metro Manila, and parts of Central Luzon, resulting in the suspension of school classes, work schedules, and flights in the area. The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology monitored the situation, issuing an Alert Level 4, indicating a hazardous explosive eruption was possible within hours to days. Volcanic activity continued into 2021, with smaller eruptions occurring in July 2021, and on March 26, 2022, a short-lived phreatomagmatic eruption was recorded. The eruptions caused significant disruptions, including the suspension of school classes, work schedules, and flights in the area, and had a major impact on the surrounding communities. Taal Volcano is a large caldera filled by Taal Lake, located in the province of Batangas, about 50 kilometers south of Manila, and is the second most active volcano in the country, with 39 confirmed historical eruptions.
